newsitem.title: HUNGARY: GM to boost globalisation with new Hungary plant.
newsitem.headline: GM to boost globalisation with new Hungary plant.

text.p: U.S. automaker General Motors Corp said on Friday that it will expand the global presence of its European-brand cars with the opening of new engine production facilities in Hungary.
German automaker Adam Opel AG, a GM subsidiary, on Friday inaugurated new operations that double its engine production capacity in Hungary to 460,000 units a year.
The additional engines will be exported to GM's car assembly plants around the world, company officials said.

"The engines will be exported to seven other European manufacturing locations, as well as to Brazil," Richard Donnelly, president of General Motors Europe AG, said at the event. The centerpiece of the new operations is a 235 million mark plant that builds engine cylinder heads that significantly raise the Hungarian value added to the engines.

Opel Hungary Ltd, launched in 1992, has exported engines to four sites in Europe and demand has grown because of the diversification of its output to include a variety of 1.4 litre and 1.6 litre Ecotec engines.

"Here in Hungary, we actually started our globalisation process (for Opel)," Louis Hughes, GM's president of international operations, said at the opening. "Hungary is and will remain one of the pillars of GM's and Opel's international strategy."
Hughes said technology from Szentgotthard will be applied in two similar facilities under construction in Australia and in Brazil.
"The experience that we gain here in Szentgotthard will be used at those other two locations," he said.
